meta.description: Power figure each chip's specifications predict, from models refitted without it, with an 80% range. 'Estimated' rows have no figure of their own; 'Held-out check' rows show how close the estimate comes where the figure is known.

sources.name: Blender Open Data benchmark snapshots
sources.licence: CC0 (Creative Commons Zero), stated on https://opendata.blender.org/download/ and in the LICENSE.txt shipped in each snapshot. No conditions on reuse; the site credits it anyway.
sources.frequency: weekly collection; snapshots are regenerated daily

limitations: The power these models learn from is rated, not measured, so 'efficiency' means points per rated watt and an estimated power figure is an estimated rating. The same code learns from measured desktop power once there is some.
Process nodes are the foundries' marketing names, used as a rough density class (pdi/tech_value/process_nodes.py). Intel 7 counts as 7 nm and TSMC 4N as 5 nm.

Every prediction comes from models refitted without the chip and without any chip with identical specifications. The 80% range is the spread of every other chip's held-out error, so it is checked, not assumed.

finding.label: prediction
finding.reason: Held-out predictions from models refitted without each chip beat the launch-year-only baseline for every kind.
